remaining.title: Hosted CI silently skips five BIND tests in internal packages
remaining.detail: The hosted e2e job installs BIND but runs only make e2e (./test/e2e ./test/interop, /home/vercel-sandbox/kudurru/Makefile:220-221) plus TestAggressiveBIND. The go job runs every package but sets only the PostgreSQL variables (ci.yml:73-75) and installs no BIND, and /home/vercel-sandbox/kudurru/hack/go-test.py:47 adds only CGO_ENABLED. So the three RPZ tests always skip there (RequireE2E at /home/vercel-sandbox/kudurru/internal/rpz/bind_test.go:100), and TestBINDSignedSecondaryThroughListeners and TestBINDStubThroughListenersAndDurableOfflineReferral skip on 'named unavailable' (secondary_signed_bind_test.go:308-311, :247-250; stub_test.go:259-262). The go job runs without -v, so the skips leave no trace in the log. The two non-RPZ skips are inferred from the workflow (the e2e job has to apt-install bind9, ci.yml:300-309), not read from a log line. Fix: add one step to the e2e job after 'Install BIND 9', for example KUDURRU_E2E=1 go test -race -count=1 -v -run '^TestBIND' ./internal/rpz ./internal/stages/authoritative ./internal/zoneview. Run 42545184734 on EPYC failed seven blocking/zone comparisons (for example stevenblack/miss p50 80 to 150 ns, suffix-1M/miss +30.4%, Lookup100k/cname p99 +52.8%), ten upstream comparisons (fast/strict +48.5%) and cache parallel hit (.context/hosted-release-73d4b057-20261109/paired-reviewed-summary.json). git diff shows no change in internal/blocking, internal/zone or internal/upstream between 73d4b057 and 9963dec2, and none between 92d5c9ee (EPYC, all 60 strategy metrics passed) and 73d4b057 (EPYC, strategies failed). My reading, which is an inference from those identical-code runs and not a measured cause: the blocking/zone and upstream failures are host noise on the EPYC VMs, which the sequential design (all reference samples, then all candidate samples, bench-paired.py:82-86) cannot cancel. Only the cache parallel-hit regression had a code cause, fixed by D348 (b176922a), and that fix has not been measured on EPYC. Work: write a decision-log entry that states the closure rule for the final run (one paired run on the final head; what happens if it draws an EPYC VM and fails) before triggering it, so the result is not interpreted after the fact. If it fails on EPYC, diagnose with the reviewed vectors before changing anything; do not raise limits or recalibrate from a failing candidate (bench/README.md closing paragraph, D335).

recommendation:
Take the hybrid route: close the cheap hosted gaps first, then do one final-head pass, and keep Knot and the dnsdist live suites as explicitly labeled local evidence for v0.2.0.

Order of work:
1. Land G23-R3 and G23-R4 as additions to the existing hosted e2e job. This follows D118 (E2E is opt-in but real, CI runs it with bind9 from apt) and the D158 fail-instead-of-skip precedent (KUDURRU_REQUIRE_POSTGRES). Both change HEAD, so they go before the benchmark.
2. Record the decision for G23-R5 (local-only labeling now, hosted jobs as a follow-up) and for G23-R6 (closure rule for the mixed EPYC/Ryzen pool) in the decision log, using the next free number after D366. Both are engineer-level choices; neither needs the owner. The runner class itself is already settled (completion-plan.md:360-366).
3. When every other v0.2.0 item has landed and CI is green on the final code SHA, run the final pass:
   a. Freeze and check: SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD); gh pr view 54 --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid must equal it; gh run list --commit "$SHA" must show ci, edge, compose, kind and security successful.

designOptions.name: Comparators A: local-only final pass
designOptions.description: Run Knot, the dnsdist live suites, the internal BIND tests and the installed-Chrome test on this machine at the final SHA and record them as local unskipped evidence; make no CI changes.
designOptions.pros: No workflow churn late in the release; images are already retained; about one hour of work.
designOptions.cons: Evidence lives in gitignored .context and depends on a /tmp Docker data root; reviewers cannot reproduce it; hosted CI keeps skipping silently on every later commit.

designOptions.name: Comparators B: move everything to hosted CI
designOptions.description: Add hosted steps or jobs for the internal BIND tests, the PostgreSQL/envtest e2e tests, Knot (private dockerd plus pulled digests) and the dnsdist live suites (constants re-pinned to the upstream dnsdist digest).
designOptions.pros: Every head, including the final one, gets unskipped comparator results with public logs; removes the single-machine dependency.
designOptions.cons: The dnsdist live fixtures were only ever run on this sandbox (host networking, UID 953 drop as root, hardcoded socket); porting them risks new hosted flakes right before release and touches ci.yml and edge.yml, which other items also edit.

designOptions.name: Comparators C: hybrid (recommended)
designOptions.description: Hosted additions for the internal BIND tests and the PostgreSQL/envtest e2e tests now (small additions to the existing e2e job); Knot and dnsdist live stay local for v0.2.0 with an explicit decision-log entry, tracker labels and a followups entry to move them to hosted CI.
designOptions.pros: Fixes the skips that cost almost nothing to fix; keeps risky fixture ports out of the release path; satisfies the 'labeled as such' rule in gaps.md:112.
designOptions.cons: Knot and dnsdist live credit still rests on one machine's retained Docker state for this release.

designOptions.name: Benchmark A: run the existing paired job once on the final head
designOptions.description: Toggle the release-benchmark-paired label and accept the outcome under the unchanged thresholds, with the closure rule written down beforehand.
designOptions.pros: Same method as the accepted 9963dec2 run; no harness change; 23 minutes.
designOptions.cons: Roughly even odds of drawing an EPYC VM, where every paired run so far has failed, in part with identical code; a failure becomes a retained failed measurement that needs a recorded follow-up.

designOptions.name: Benchmark B: interleave reference and candidate samples before the final run
designOptions.description: Change bench-paired.py to alternate reference and candidate processes per suite instead of running all reference samples and then all candidate samples, update hack/test_bench_paired.py, record the change in the decision log, then run on the final head.
designOptions.pros: Cancels slow host drift, which is the likely cause of the EPYC upstream and miss-path failures; thresholds, limits, workloads and the reference commit stay unchanged.
designOptions.cons: Changes the measurement control just before the deciding run, which can read as moving the goalposts; the reference collector assumes a full separate recording, so this is a real refactor with control-test changes; earlier runs are no longer methodologically identical.

risks: Runner pool lottery: the paired run passed blocking/zone and upstream only on Ryzen 9 7950X3D VMs and failed on every EPYC 9454P VM (three runs), twice with unchanged code in the failing packages. A single final-head run may fail for reasons unrelated to the release, and the project's own rules forbid retrying or replacing a failed sample.
Cache parallel-hit after D348 has never been measured on EPYC; the only evidence is a local diagnostic (237.7 to 164.8 ns, completion-plan.md:1265-1267) and the Ryzen pass.

The dnsdist live suites depend on a locally built image ID inside /tmp/kudurru-lab-docker-data; a VM rebuild or /tmp cleanup removes the only copy and the tests then fail until their constants are changed.

Label trigger subtleties: the 'labeled' event fires only on add, so the label must be removed first; a re-run of an old workflow run re-measures the old head SHA from the event payload, not the new head; any label added to PR #54 by someone else starts another run in the same concurrency group and can displace a pending one.
workflow_dispatch is unproven: benchmarks.yml is not on main and all seven runs were label-triggered; the gh token shows no scope header, so actions:write cannot be confirmed without dispatching.

The final-head requirement is fragile: one more non-docs commit after the paired run or the local comparator pass voids them. hack/ci-changes.sh treats docs-only commits as non-code, which is the only safe follow-up.

Hosted go shards run without -v, so skipped comparators are invisible in their logs; the claim that the two non-RPZ internal BIND tests skip there rests on the workflow not installing BIND in that job, not on a log line.

The working tree has a modified /home/vercel-sandbox/kudurru/dashboard/dist/index.html. The collector refuses a dirty checkout (bench-release.py:171-172) if anyone runs it locally, and the Knot test hard-links a binary built from the working tree.

Local comparator runs share 8 CPUs and one Docker daemon with other work; the F18c held-CNAME test and the anchor/edge tests have 5-second and similar deadlines that have failed under load before (completion-plan.md:113).
Local BIND is 9.18.50 while hosted is 9.18.39; results from the two are not the same program build and should be recorded with their versions.
